calls.head: Don’t buy Vasilevskiy’s record against the Islanders
calls.body: Vasilevskiy has been a wall against the Islanders since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Vasilevskiy isn’t that wall tonight.

calls.head: Expect the Lightning to have the puck more
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Lightning have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Islanders around the middle. The ice should tilt the Lightning’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

TBL.head: We gave Tampa Bay a 64% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: The Islanders’ power play came alive
surprises.body: The Islanders have had one of the league’s least effective power plays for years, and Tampa Bay kills penalties better than most. Not tonight: the Islanders’ power play created 16.2 expected goals per 60, against their usual 6.8 (about 6.4 against Tampa Bay) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: Hagel lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Jake Guentzel opened the scoring for the Lightning early in the first, and Brandon Hagel made it 2-0 late in the period. It was a busy second period. Tony DeAngelo got the Islanders on the board early in the period. Guentzel scored again on the power play a minute and a half later to make it 3-1 for the Lightning. Midway through the second, Scott Sabourin and Logan Stanley squared off, and Jean-Gabriel Pageau pulled the Isles within one. Brayden Schenn tied it up on the power play with just seven seconds left in the second, but that was the last goal the Islanders would get. Hagel scored his second of the night with less than two minutes left to put the Lightning ahead for good. Hagel completed his hat trick into the empty net with less than two minutes left.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 20 saves for the Lightning, and Ilya Sorokin stopped 21 of 25 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Matthew Schaefer had the best night of anyone, even in a loss and with Hagel’s hat trick in the game. The Lightning moved to 4-1-0 and climbed into first in the Atlantic, while the Islanders fell to 2-3-0, slipping to seventh in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Lightning.
Jake Guentzel scored twice more against the Islanders, and has eight goals in ten games against them since 2023-24.
Nikita Kucherov has a point in every game this season.
Jean-Gabriel Pageau scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 9.
